question: Using the definition of ADS and Table 5A-1, explain why Level 2 is not an ADS level while Level 3 is.
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD defines an Automated Driving System (ADS) as hardware and software capable of performing the *entire* Dynamic Driving Task (DDT) on a sustained basis, a term used specifically for Level 3, 4, or 5 systems. At Level 2, the system executes only steering and acceleration/deceleration while "the human driver performs all remaining aspects of the Dynamic Driving Task," so it does not perform the entire DDT and Table 5A-1 categorizes it as ADAS. At Level 3, the system provides "sustained performance by an ADS of all aspects of the Dynamic Driving Task within a given ODD," meeting the full-DDT definition, so Table 5A-1 places it in the Automated Driving System (ADS) category. Standards (mandatory): - Per the acronym list, when used in this Manual "ADS" shall mean "Automated Driving System" (Section 1C.03). Support (informational, from the definitions and table): - "Automated Driving System (ADS) – The hardware and software that are collectively capable of performing the entire Dynamic Driving Task (DDT) on a sustained basis, regardless of whether it is limited to a specific Operational Design Domain (ODD); this term is used specifically to describe a Level 3, 4, or 5 driving automation system." - "Automation Levels – The levels of automation that are described in Table 5A-1." - Table 5A-1, Level 2: "The driving mode specific execution by one or more sustained driver assistance systems of both steering and acceleration/deceleration … with the expectation that the human driver performs all remaining aspects of the Dynamic Driving Task" — Automation Category: Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS). - Table 5A-1, Level 3: "The driving mode specific sustained performance by an ADS of all aspects of the Dynamic Driving Task within a given ODD with the expectation that the human driver will respond appropriately to a request to intervene" — Automation Category: Automated Driving System (ADS). Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 5A-1, where the "Automation Category" column groups Levels 1–2 under "Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS)" and Levels 3–5 under "Automated Driving System (ADS)," with all of Levels 1–5 sharing the "Driving Automation System" automation type. [Image 2] shows the Section 5A.03 definition of ADS (Item B), which restricts the term to systems performing the entire DDT and to Levels 3, 4, or 5. [Image 4] shows the Chapter 5A general text, including the Section 5A.03 lead-in stating the definitions come from SAE J3016 and the ADAS definition (Item A) describing systems that merely aid the driver with one or more driving tasks. Citations: - Section 5A.03 Support §1 (p.760) - Table 5A-1 (p.760) - Section 1C.03 Standard §1 (p.31) - Section 5A.02 Support §1 (p.759) - Page 801 - Page 800
gold_answer: An ADS performs the entire dynamic driving task on a sustained basis and the term applies to Levels 3-5. Level 2 performs steering and acceleration/deceleration but still expects the human to perform all remaining aspects of the task, so it is ADAS rather than ADS. Level 3 performs all aspects within its ODD, subject to a human fallback request.
